Practical SQL knowledge — correct SELECT/WHERE syntax, understanding of DELETE vs. TRUNCATE, and comfort writing simple queries against a relational schema
Core data structures knowledge — arrays vs. linked lists, when to use a stack or a queue, and basic algorithmic problem-solving
Object-oriented programming fundamentals — inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes vs. interfaces, explained with real examples
Operating systems basics — what a process is, fundamentals of multithreading and memory management
Strong quantitative aptitude — time-and-work, ratios, percentages, and logical/seating-arrangement style reasoning
Clear communication and a collaborative attitude — comfortable explaining your final-year project and working under deadline pressure
Awareness of the software development lifecycle and the difference between Agile and Waterfall, and why documentation matters
Perform unit testing and collaborate closely with QA
Document your work clearly for future maintainers; why documentation matters
Enterprise-grade banking and financial services products such as FLEXCUBE and OBDX
